subject: Next steps: competitive evaluation + reservation path for dedicated capacity
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@medsys.ai>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Quick follow-up + proposed test matrix from today's call

Elena — thanks again for the time earlier. Good call; appreciate the clarity around your production constraints and peak patterns. Two quick notes and a suggested set of next steps so we keep momentum: 

1) Summary of what you shared (re: capacity needs):
- Primary workload: clinical note ingestion -> summarization + entity extraction; average req size ~1.2k tokens, 95th ~3k tokens.
- Traffic shape: steady baseline ~18 req/s with predictable nightly spikes (2-3x) and occasional burst events up to ~180 req/s during batch sends.
- Latency target: p95 <= 250ms for short requests, acceptable up to 600ms for long-context jobs.
- Security: VPC + customer-managed KMS required; SOC2 evidence requested.

2) Competitive angle you mentioned: you are evaluating both hyperscaler reserved GPUs (committed instance pools) and Redwood Dedicated. Key decision factors you listed: predictability of sustained throughput, cost under burst, fallback behavior during cloud preemption, and ease of compliance evidence.

3) Proposed test matrix (fast, pragmatically scoped):
A) Steady-state throughput: 18 req/s sustained for 1 hour at avg request size (1.2k) — measure p50/p95/p99 latency, token cost.
B) Spiky bursts: 3x baseline for 30 minutes with bursts to 200 req/s for 2 minutes every 10 minutes — evaluate autoscale behavior & queuing.
C) Long-context run: 8k token window on 10 concurrent requests to measure memory usage and tail latencies.
D) Failover exercise: simulate a node preemption and observe Redwood fallback to pre-warmed pool and model variant with quantized weights.

I'm attaching a short cheat sheet that contrasts reserved hyperscaler paths vs Redwood Dedicated (ops assumptions, typical SLA behaviors, and cost levers). Can we lock a 2–3 hour slot next week for a hands-on benchmark with your infra team and our SEs (Camila + me)?

Proposed slots: Tue 2027-04-13 10:00–12:00 PT, Wed 2027-04-14 09:00–11:00 PT. Tell me which works and I'll send a calendar invite + test harness (JMeter load profile + example dataset).

Thanks,
Markus
Markus Klein
Sr. Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
markus@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-vs-hyperscaler-cheatsheet.pdf
From: Elena Morales <elena@medsys.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@medsys.ai
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up + proposed test matrix from today's call

Markus — thanks for the recap and the clear test plan. That matrix looks like exactly what we need to separate the operational behaviors. A few clarifications from our side before we schedule: 

- For the spiky bursts (B), we care about cold-starts during sudden ramp from 25 -> 200 req/s; hyperscaler approach would usually rely on instance warm pools but there’s no consistent pre-warm across zones for us today. Will Redwood guarantee warm replicas or is that part of a dedicated contract?
- For the failover test (D), we need to see audit logs and a step-by-step timeline — SEC & compliance require chain-of-events for any preemption/fallback.
- Budget note: our procurement prefers a 12-month reserved path if unit economics beat on-demand by at least 30%. If Redwood Dedicated shows a cost delta of <20% vs reserved hyperscaler it will be hard to justify the migration.

We can do Wed 2027-04-14 09:00–11:00 PT; ops@ will join. Please include an estimate of test time cost and the specific SLO language you propose for the dedicated offering (latency p95/p99, availability, and maintenance blackout windows).

Thanks,
Elena
VP Engineering, MedSys Health
Elena.Morales@medsys.ai
From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: markus@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: prep for MedSys benchmark — responsibilities and deliverables

Quick internal note to prepare the Wed run. Action items: 
- Camila: bring the JMeter profiles and the quantized model variant for the 8k run. Prepare a short demo script showing how fallback to quantized variant impacts latency/cost.
- Markus: draft a one-page SLO/contract blurb (p95/p99 + availability) and a short procurement-friendly cost comparison (12-month reserved hyperscaler vs Redwood Dedicated TCO). Use the medsys token assumptions Elena gave.
- Ops: I'll spin up the test harness in our staging Dedicated cluster (us-west-2). Need the sample dataset + an API key from Elena's ops account — Markus, can you confirm they will share?

I'll compile results into a short deck during the run. Camila — can you confirm you have the SOC2 cert fragment we can share (redacted) for the meeting?

—Aditya
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.ai>

Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, camila_reyes@redwood.ai, ops@medsys.ai
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 10:18:00 -0700

Elena — great, Wed 09:00–11:00 PT confirmed. Short meeting agenda and what we'll bring (so procurement knows expectations):

Agenda (90m):
1) 09:00–09:10 — Introductions + success criteria (you)
2) 09:10–09:40 — Run A & B (steady + spiky) — measure p50/p95/p99, queueing, and autoscale timeliness
3) 09:40–10:10 — Run C (long-context 8k) — memory/throughput validation and model-variant tradeoffs
4) 10:10–10:30 — Failover demo & audit timeline (preemption -> fallback)
5) 10:30–10:50 — Procurement checklist / high-level TCO comparison (12-month reserved hypothetical)
6) 10:50–11:00 — Actions & next steps (PO timing, contract template path)

What we'll provide in advance (attached + links):
- Short cheatsheet comparing reserved hyperscaler vs Redwood Dedicated (attached).
- Draft SLO blurb: p95 <= 250ms (short), p99 <= 800ms (long-context), availability SLA 99.95% with maintenance windows noted.
- TCO assumptions: token mix from your notes, GPU unit rates for reserved hyperscaler vs Redwood Dedicated projected over 12 months. I’ll share a one-page comparison during the call.

What we need from you before Wed:
- Test API key (ops@) or a whitelisted IP so we can run from your staging (secure exchange via our SSO/Drive link).
- Confirmation on the dataset sample (anonymized batch of 500 records).

Attachments: medsys-reqs-2027.xlsx (your supplied traffic assumptions) — please confirm it contains the correct token distribution.

If procurement wants deeper financial modeling, we can commit to a 3-path quote: On-demand, 12-month reserved (hyperscaler), and Redwood Dedicated reserved (12-month) with committed throughput pricing. We'll include breakpoints where Redwood remits credits if burst capacity constraints are hit (we've done this before for other customers).

See you Wed — sending calendar invite now.

Cheers,
Markus
